proposals.before: In the first year of Kaiping under the Liang, he was given the additional titles of Grand Guardian and concurrent Palace Attendant.
proposals.after: In the first year of Kaiping under the Liang, he was given the additional titles of Acting Grand Commandant and concurrent Palace Attendant.
proposals.reason: 檢校太尉 is Acting Grand Commandant/Grand Marshal, not Grand Guardian (太保).

proposals.before: In the first year of Kaiping of Liang, he was given the additional titles of Grand Guardian and concurrent Palace Attendant.
proposals.after: In the first year of Kaiping of Liang, he was given the additional titles of Acting Grand Commandant and concurrent Palace Attendant.
proposals.reason: Same error: 太尉 misrendered as Grand Guardian.

proposals.before: Yan, who had originally borne the name Yan, was Qian’s son by a concubine.
proposals.after: Yan (龑), who had originally borne the name Yan (巖), was Qian’s son by a concubine.
proposals.reason: English collapses distinct characters 龑 and 巖 into identical 'Yan', obscuring the renaming.

proposals.before: He also contended westward with Ma Yin over Rong and Gui; Yin took the Gui circuit and captured Shizheng;
proposals.after: He also contended westward with Ma Yin over Rong and Gui; Ma Yin took the Gui circuit and captured Shizheng;
proposals.reason: Bare 'Yin' after Ma Yin wrongly looks like Liu Yin; Chinese 殷取桂管 refers to Ma Yin.

proposals.before: Liu Changlu of Gaozhou, Liu Qian of Xinzhou, and more than seventy stockades east of the river — none of them could be brought under control.
proposals.after: Liu Changlu of Gaozhou, Liu Qian (劉潛) of Xinzhou, and more than seventy stockades east of the river — none of them could be brought under control.
proposals.reason: English 'Liu Qian' for 劉潛 collides with Liu Yin's father 謙; disambiguate the given name.

proposals.before: Kezhen also attacked and took the capital of Jiaozhi, plundered its treasures, and returned.
proposals.after: Kezhen also attacked Champa (占城), plundered its treasures, and returned.
proposals.reason: 占城 is Champa, not the capital of Jiaozhi; the idiomatic rendering invents Jiaozhi.

proposals.before: Yan’s original name was Yan; he later changed it to Zhi.
proposals.after: Yan’s original name was Yan (巖); he later changed it to Zhi (陟).
proposals.reason: English collapses distinct personal names 巖 and 陟 into ambiguous Yan.

proposals.before: In the fifth year he enfeoffed his sons: Yaoshu as Prince of Yong, Guitu as Prince of Kang, Hongdu as Prince of Qin, Hongxi as Prince of Jin, Hongchang as Prince of Yue, Hongbi as Prince of Qi, Hongya as Prince of Shao, Hongze as Prince of Zhen, Hongcao as Prince of Wan, Honggao as Prince of Xun, Hongwei as Prince of Xi, Hongmiao as Prince of Gao, Hong Jian as Prince of Tong, Hong Jian as Prince of Yi, Hongji as Prince of Bian, Hongdao as Prince of Gui, Hongzhao as Prince of Xuan, Hongzheng as Prince of Tong, and Hongyi as Prince of Ding.
proposals.after: In the fifth year he enfeoffed his sons: Yaoshu as Prince of Yong, Guitu as Prince of Kang, Hongdu as Prince of Qin, Hongxi as Prince of Jin, Hongchang as Prince of Yue, Hongbi as Prince of Qi, Hongya as Prince of Shao, Hongze as Prince of Zhen, Hongcao as Prince of Wan, Honggao as Prince of Xun, Hongwei as Prince of Xi, Hongmiao as Prince of Gao, Hongjian (洪簡) as Prince of Tong (同), Hongjian (洪建) as Prince of Yi, Hongji as Prince of Bian, Hongdao as Prince of Gui, Hongzhao as Prince of Xuan, Hongzheng as Prince of Tong, and Hongyi as Prince of Ding.
proposals.reason: English collapses 洪簡 and 洪建 into identical 'Hong Jian' and blurs 同王 vs later 通王.

proposals.before: In the fifth year Sheng’s younger brothers Hongbi, Hongdao, Hongyi, Hongji, Hong Jian, Hong Jian, Hongwei, and Hongzhao were all killed on the same day.
proposals.after: In the fifth year Sheng’s younger brothers Hongbi, Hongdao, Hongyi, Hongji, Hongjian (洪簡), Hongjian (洪建), Hongwei, and Hongzhao were all killed on the same day.
proposals.reason: Identical English 'Hong Jian' for distinct 洪簡 and 洪建.

decisions.reason: 檢校太尉 is Acting Grand Commandant; Grand Guardian would translate 太保, a different office.
The literal field contains the same confusion of 太尉 with 太保.

decisions.after: Yan, whose original name was a homophonous Yan written with a different character, was Qian's son by a concubine.
decisions.reason: The source distinguishes the later name from the original homophone. This wording makes the renaming intelligible without inserting Chinese characters into the English field.
Repeating Ma Yin's full name resolves the otherwise misleading bare 'Yin,' which can be read as the chapter's main subject Liu Yin.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 與馬殷爭容、桂，殷取桂管

decisions.reason: Liu Qian is an accurate and unambiguous personal name in this sentence. Adding Chinese characters solely because another person elsewhere has the homophonous name Qian is unnecessary.

decisions.after: Kezhen also attacked Champa, plundered its treasures, and returned.
decisions.reason: 占城 is Champa, not the capital of Jiaozhi. The revision corrects the place without inserting Chinese characters into the English field.

decisions.after: Yan's original name was a homophonous Yan written with a different character; he later changed it to Zhi.
decisions.reason: The English needs to convey that the first two names are written differently despite sharing a pronunciation; the proposed Chinese annotations are not appropriate inside the English field.
The proposal inserts Chinese characters into the English field. The distinct princely titles and the facing source list already distinguish the two homophonous Hongjian names.
The proposed parenthetical characters are not valid English-field content. The source-facing presentation preserves which two homophonous brothers are meant.
